questions.question:
**The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.**

The man whose sitting at the corner table is my uncle.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'whose sitting'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, '**who is sitting**' should be used instead of '**whose sitting**'.
 
• '**Who**' is a **subject pronoun** that is used to describe who performed an action or who is in a specific state.
 
• '**Whose**' is a **possessive pronoun** that refers to the person to whom something belongs.
 
• Here, in the given sentence '**who**' is referring to the subject '**the man**'.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.****
 

Correct Sentence:__** *The man **who is sitting **at the corner table is my uncle.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** 

 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहां **'whose sitting'** के स्थान पर **'who is sitting'** का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
 
• '**Who**' एक** subject pronoun **है जिसका उपयोग यह वर्णन करने के लिए किया जाता है कि किसने कार्रवाई की या किसी विशिष्ट स्थिति में कौन है।
 
• '**Whose**' एक **possession pronoun **है जो उस व्यक्ति को संदर्भित करता है जिसके पास कुछ है।
 
• यहाँ, दिए गए वाक्य में '**who**' विषय '**the man**' की बात कर रहा है।
 
• अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है।

While listing N consecutive even numbers for determining their average, the last number, by mistake, got replaced by the next odd number and thereby the average turned out to be more than the desired value by 0.0125. What is the value of N?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The next odd number after any even number L is L + 1.

Total Increase in Sum = (L + 1) − L = 1.

Increase in Average = (Total Increase in Sum) ÷ (Number of Terms N).

0.0125 = 1 ÷ N

N = 1 ÷ 0.0125 = 80.

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of consecutive even numbers = N

Error: Last even number replaced by next odd number

Increase in average = 0.0125

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e60de71f8d76c81c51127486d8316eaf7d0f398414175c6dfe74df0cbb3a51f6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the N consecutive even numbers be E₁, E₂, ..., EN.

⇒ Let their original sum be S.

⇒ Original Average = S ÷ N.

⇒ The last number EN is replaced by (EN + 1).

⇒ New Sum = S − EN + (EN + 1) = S + 1.

⇒ New Average = (S + 1) ÷ N = (S ÷ N) + (1 ÷ N).

⇒ Change in average = (New Average) − (Original Average) = 1 ÷ N.

⇒ Given that this change is 0.0125.

⇒ 1 ÷ N = 0.0125

⇒ N = 1 ÷ 0.0125

⇒ N = 10000 ÷ 125 = 80.

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effect of Observation Change on Average

If a single observation in a set of N terms is increased by 'k', the new average increases by exactly k ÷ N compared to the old average.

Consecutive Even Numbers

Consecutive even numbers form an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with a common difference of 2. The average of any N consecutive numbers in an AP is (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Decimal to Fraction Conversion

Shortcut for N: Since 0.125 = 1/8, then 0.0125 = 1/80. Therefore, 1 ÷ N = 1 ÷ 80 implies N = 80.</p

questions.question: The mean of a set of 120 observations is 80. 10 is subtracted from each observation and each of the corresponding result is divided by 7. What is the mean of the new set?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Arithmetic Mean** follows the same linear transformations as the individual observations.

Initial **Mean** = 80

Step 1 (Subtraction): 80 − 10 = 70

Step 2 (Division): 70 ÷ 7 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **observations** (n) = 120

Original **Mean** (µₒₗd) = 80

**Formula Used:**

If each observation xᵢ is transformed to yᵢ = (xᵢ − a) ÷ b, then New Mean (µₙₑw) = (µₒₗd − a) ÷ b

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/507c63d038b9653c1efdb58472edcc76a0fc31dd1f6affad09fd2f2f08c935e5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of original 120 observations (∑xᵢ) = 120 × 80 = 9600

⇒ New observations result from subtracting 10: ∑(xᵢ − 10) = 9600 − (120 × 10) = 9600 − 1200 = 8400

⇒ Each result is then divided by 7: ∑[(xᵢ − 10) ÷ 7] = 8400 ÷ 7 = 1200

⇒ **New Mean** = New Total Sum ÷ Number of observations

⇒ **New Mean** = 1200 ÷ 120 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Change of Origin

If a constant k is added to or subtracted from every value in a dataset, the **mean** increases or decreases by the same constant k.

Change of Scale

If every value in a dataset is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant k, the **mean** is also multiplied or divided by k.

Combined Mean Formula

For two sets with means x₁ and x₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂, the combined mean is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: In case of a particular transaction, the profit earned is 14(2)/({7)}%. What fraction is the cost price of the selling price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Profit %** to fraction: 14 2/7% = 1/7.

Here, **Denominator (7)** represents the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Numerator (1)** represents the **Profit**.

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP + Profit = 7 + 1 = 8 units.

Required fraction (**CP/SP**) = 7/8.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Profit percentage** = 14 2/7% = (100/7)%.

**Formula Used:** **Selling Price (SP)** = Cost Price (CP) + Profit; **Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28b501e38afd97887adce4e336cad9cdf108c3ac421156f4089ae720b2a59df3.png] 

⇒ **Profit fraction** = (100/7) ÷ 100 = 1/7

⇒ This implies that for every 7 units of **Cost Price**, the **Profit** earned is 1 unit.

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 7x

⇒ **Profit** = 1x

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = CP + Profit = 7x + 1x = 8x

⇒ **Fraction of CP to SP** = CP ÷ SP = 7x ÷ 8x

⇒ **Fraction** = 7/8

**∴ The correct answer is 7/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Common percentages like 14 2/7% = 1/7, 12 1/2% = 1/8, and 11 1/9% = 1/9 are essential for solving **Profit and Loss** questions quickly.

CP and SP Relationship

If **Profit %** is expressed as a fraction a/b, then the ratio of **CP : SP** is always b : (b + a). For a **Loss %** of a/b, the ratio of **CP : SP** is b : (b − a).

Marked Price and Discount

**Selling Price** can also be calculated using **Marked Price (MP)**: SP = MP × (1 − Discount%/100).</p

• **P = mgh**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• The energy obtained by an object by virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.
 
 
• **KE = (1)/(2) times mv²**
 
 
 
• K is kinetic energy, v is the speed of the object, and m is the mass of the object.
